USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Drug properties affecting response: 1

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

Two medicines have similar target affinity but differ markedly in passage across lipid membranes. One reaches the CNS more readily because of its physicochemical properties. Which drug characteristic most directly contributes to this difference?

  1. Lipid solubility and membrane passage
  2. Molecular size limiting passive membrane passage
  3. Formulation-dependent release
  4. Additive pharmacodynamic effects
  5. Complex formation reducing absorption
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Lipid solubility and membrane passage

Physicochemical properties influence membrane penetration, distribution and sometimes CNS entry.

Understanding the options

Lipid solubility and membrane passage
Physicochemical properties influence membrane penetration, distribution and sometimes CNS entry.
Molecular size limiting passive membrane passage
Large molecules often cross lipid membranes poorly without specialized transport or delivery. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Formulation-dependent release
Immediate- and modified-release products can have different concentration-time profiles despite containing the same drug. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Additive pharmacodynamic effects
Two medicines with similar physiological actions can increase the combined effect or toxicity. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Complex formation reducing absorption
Binding of some medicines to polyvalent cations can reduce gastrointestinal absorption. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
